description:
Grammar sweep: the reduced case for each divergence the generated grammar sweep found, one
per root cause, so each finding is pinned by the smallest script that shows it.

cases.name: gram minimal C2-01: expansion after a here-document operator on the same line
gram minimal C2-02: recursive function thirty calls deep
cases.script: d() { if [ $1 -gt 0 ]; then d $(($1-1)); fi; }; d 30; echo ok

cases.name: gram minimal C2-03: arithmetic command error continues the list
gram minimal C2-04: arithmetic constant too great for its base
gram minimal C2-05: associative element in arithmetic
gram minimal C2-06: quotes inside arithmetic
gram minimal C2-07: legacy arithmetic with a subscript and a comparison
gram minimal C2-08: subscript with an operator in an assignment word
gram minimal C2-09: nameref to an array element
cases.script: a=(x y); declare -n r='a[1]'; echo "[$r]"; r=z; echo "${a[1]}"

cases.name: gram minimal C2-10: self-referencing nameref
gram minimal C2-11: readonly array element assignment
gram minimal C2-12: readonly assignment in arithmetic
gram minimal C2-13: unset of a quoted associative key
gram minimal C2-14: associative array key order
gram minimal C2-15: unset of every element with an at subscript
gram minimal C2-16: read into an array element
gram minimal C2-17: exported array in a child shell
gram minimal C2-18: export of an expanded assignment
gram minimal C2-19: key-value transform of an associative array
gram minimal C2-20: case toggle operator
gram minimal C2-21: bad substitution
gram minimal C2-22: shortest trim with a star
gram minimal C2-23: ampersand in a pattern replacement
gram minimal C2-24: alternative of an empty array
gram minimal C2-25: assignment operator on a positional parameter
gram minimal C2-26: length of the status parameter
gram minimal C2-27: prefix names include declared unset variables
gram minimal C2-28: indirection through an invalid name
gram minimal C2-29: character class against a non-ASCII letter
gram minimal C2-30: octal escape above 255
gram minimal C2-31: escaped dollar inside backquotes
gram minimal C2-32: case statement inside command substitution
cases.script: echo $(case a in a) echo m;; esac)

cases.name: gram minimal C2-33: function substitution
gram minimal C2-34: letter sequence across punctuation
gram minimal C2-35: read with an escaped IFS character
gram minimal C2-36: mapfile callback
gram minimal C2-37: exit with too many arguments
gram minimal C2-38: break with a zero count in nested loops
cases.script: for i in 1 2; do for j in a b; do break 0; done; echo $i; done; echo "end $?"

cases.name: gram minimal C2-39: break in a pipeline stage
cases.script: for i in 1 2; do echo x | break; echo $i; done

cases.name: gram minimal C2-40: kill of a subshell by BASHPID
gram minimal C2-41: BASH_SUBSHELL in a pipeline stage
gram minimal C2-42: nested subshell with a space
gram minimal C2-43: failed redirection on a group
gram minimal C2-44: noclobber and the both-streams operator
cases.script: cd /tmp; echo old > f; set -C; echo new &> f; echo "status=$?"; cat f

cases.name: gram minimal C2-45: line continuation in a here-document
gram minimal C2-46: alias ending in a space
cases.script:
shopt -s expand_aliases
alias run='echo run '
alias w=word
run w

cases.name: gram minimal C2-47: alias value with a lone quote
gram minimal C2-48: DEBUG trap before arithmetic and conditional commands
gram minimal C2-49: RETURN trap after source
gram minimal C2-50: ERR trap for a failing group
gram minimal C2-51: EXIT trap when killed by TERM
cases.script: trap 'echo cleanup' EXIT; kill -TERM $$; echo after

cases.name: gram minimal C2-52: unset last background pid under nounset
gram minimal C2-53: PS4 expansion
gram minimal C2-54: empty TIMEFORMAT
gram minimal C2-55: dot without a file name
gram minimal C2-56: printed function with a here-document sourced back
gram minimal C2-57: test with -o and -a precedence
gram minimal C2-58: GLOBIGNORE with a bracket pattern
cases.script: cd /tmp; : > a; : > b; : > c; GLOBIGNORE='[ab]'; echo *

cases.name: gram minimal C2-59: globstar after a directory star
cases.script: cd /tmp; mkdir -p d; : > d/f; : > g; shopt -s globstar; echo */**

cases.name: gram minimal C2-60: negated extglob against the empty string
gram minimal C2-61: failglob inside a function
cases.script: shopt -s failglob; f() { echo nomatch*; echo in-f; }; f; echo "status=$?"

cases.name: gram minimal C2-62: for with an invalid variable name
cases.script: for 1x in a; do echo "[$1x]"; done; echo "status=$?"

cases.name: gram minimal C2-63: return in a pipeline stage
cases.script: f() { echo x | return 5; echo "after $?"; }; f

cases.name: gram minimal C2-64: caller in a command string
gram minimal C2-65: export of a name without a value
gram minimal C2-66: test -ef on a missing file
gram minimal C2-67: redirection to an empty file name
gram minimal C2-68: kill -l of an exit status
gram minimal C2-69: close redirection followed by a word
gram minimal C2-70: negation after a pipe
gram minimal C2-71: assignment with a failed redirection
gram minimal C2-72: set dash turns off xtrace
gram minimal C2-73: USR1 trap
cases.script: trap 'echo usr1' USR1; kill -USR1 $$; echo after

cases.name: gram minimal C2-74: here-document expansion side effect with cat
gram minimal C2-75: local nameref named like its target
cases.script: f() { local -n v=v; v=x; }; v=orig; f; echo "$v"

cases.name: gram minimal C2-76: mapfile with an invalid array name
gram minimal C2-77: lowercase and uppercase attributes together
gram minimal C2-78: status seen by a RETURN trap
gram minimal C2-79: EXIT trap in a command substitution
cases.script: x=$(trap 'echo cs-exit' EXIT; echo in); echo "[$x]"

cases.name: gram minimal C2-80: uppercasing sharp s
gram minimal C2-81: empty associative key
gram minimal C2-82: read of zero characters
gram minimal C2-83: ANSI-C quote inside a double-quoted default
gram minimal C2-84: read with blanks around a non-blank IFS delimiter
cases.script: IFS=': ' read -r k v <<< 'key : value'; echo "[$k] [$v]"
